newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK PMI survey and August M0 data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK PMI survey and August M0 data.

text.p: Following is a list of reactions to the UK purchasing managers survey and M0 data for August published at 0930 GMT.
The PMI survey read 51.8 in August, the highest level in a year. M0 rose a seasonally adjusted 7.5 percent y/y in August.

"This shows the good news on retail spending we've seen recently is having a beneficial effect on manufacturers. We have been looking for a second half pick-up. It looks as though that is now coming through. It's less easy now for the Chancellor to justify any further interest rate cuts." (RFTV)

"The PMI and M0 data for August provide further evidence that the UK economy is in the process of recovery. These data should be a small negative for the UK interest rate markets and a small positive for the pound. We doubt that the Chancellor will take the risk with a cut in rates when he meets with the Governor of the Bank of England on Wednesday so we would expect this pattern of price movement to continue through to the second half of the week."

"The Chancellor still has quite a lot of ammunition in his favour. But today's figures will certainly reinforce the cautious stance of Mr George and don't suggest an interest rate cut is definite on Wednesday but I still wouldn't rule it out. The correlation between M0 and retail sales hasn't been that good. This doesn't rule out a rate cut. The last opportune time would be next month."

"The PMI survey is very encouraging indeed. We are finally seeing signs that the pick up in consumer activity is feeding right the way through the economy with production of intermediate up, orders up and output up. This really underpins what the Bank of England has been saying that the whole economy is starting to turn round. The chances of another rate cut are really falling by the wayside. The prices balance is up, but that was expected and not too worrying."
